summary: Self-hosted system of agents that watch the web, feeds and inboxes and act for you, including AI text and image steps.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Huginn lets you build agents that do automated tasks for you online. Agents read websites, watch feeds and mailboxes, react to events and take actions such as sending alerts or posting messages, and they can use OpenAI-compatible APIs to summarise, classify or translate text.
sixtySeconds.problem: Keeping an eye on websites, feeds and services by hand is tedious, and hosted automation tools see all your data. Huginn runs on your own server and chains small agents together into your own automations.
whoFor: Self-hosters who want their own automation server
Developers wiring up web and API workflows
People tracking prices, news or site changes
Teams sending alerts to Slack or Telegram
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a mature, self-hosted alternative to hosted automation services, with agents that pass events to each other and optional AI steps.

overview: Agents create and consume events and pass them along a directed graph. Examples in the README: scrape websites and email you on changes, watch RSS feeds, IMAP mailboxes, webhooks and MQTT, track the weather, send digests, post to Slack or Telegram, and summarise, classify, translate or generate images and speech through OpenAI-compatible APIs.

The quickest trial is the official Docker image; log in as admin with the password printed once in the container log. For production, the README recommends Docker Compose with MySQL or PostgreSQL, and there is a manual install guide for Ubuntu or Debian.

steps.title: Log in
steps.body: Open http://localhost:3000 and log in as admin with the password printed once in the container log.

steps.title: Use the official Compose setup
steps.body: Runs the web process and worker with MySQL or PostgreSQL. See the Docker documentation in the repository for persistent storage.

firstRun.title: Create your first agent
firstRun.body: In the web UI, add a Website Agent that watches a page and connect it to an Email Agent.

tutorial.title: Get an email when a website changes
tutorial.useCase: Chain two agents: one watches a page, one sends you an email.

steps.title: Add a Website Agent
steps.body: Point it at the page and the part you want to watch.

steps.title: Add an Email Agent
steps.body: Make it receive events from the Website Agent.
